A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete matching main text, equations, four figures, ten tables and Appendices A-D. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original classifier experiments and data analyses in Section 7 and Appendices A-B, plus convergence experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains those original DCP/minDCP experiments, data analyses and convergence results in Section 7 and Appendices A-D.

M1.justification: The DCP bounding methods, sequential linear programming algorithm, greedy initialization and treatment of unknown confusion matrices are unchanged, including Appendices C-D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate US Census and Natality classifiers, UK election changes and US education transitions, with identical protected attributes and known/unknown confusion-matrix scenarios.

E2.justification: Section 7.1 and the corresponding tables retain Average, Greedy, Average+LM and Greedy+LM in the same comparisons. No comparator is added, removed or revised.

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures and settings match throughout. For example, Section 7 retains the neural network's 64/32-unit layers, learning rate 0.001, batch size 256 and four epochs, and Natality's nine-neighbor classifier.

E4.justification: The initialization comparisons, aggregate-data case studies and Appendix D convergence analysis across trust-region sizes are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Appendix C retains ten random label orderings per upper-bound calculation; neither version reports additional seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1-10 and the empirical plots match. For example, Table 10 retains education-transition bounds of 2.38%, 2.94%, 2.22% and 2.32%.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 4.1 and its proof, bounding derivations, and mathematical development in Appendices C-D are identical apart from typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about multiclass DCP, interpretable fairness auditing, estimation under two information regimes and empirical accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including bound tightness, convergence to local minima, fairness-criterion suitability and caution when upper and lower bounds are far apart.

D1.justification: Implementation libraries, hyperparameters, numerical stabilization, trust-region settings and code/data access information match. The code and data hyperlinks retain their destinations.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to binary DCP and prior multiclass fairness research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, 31 July 2025, to v4, 9 October 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are tiny spacing/alignment shifts in displayed equations, including Equations (8)-(9). Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-10 retain their content, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves v3's scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The updated version/date stamp and negligible typesetting shifts do not materially change clarity, correctness or evidential support.
